question.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}+2x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x+2 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))(2x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x-2\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+2(x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-2D.$
